title: PwC is hiring fewer consultants and accountants. Its CEO is still sending his kids into consulting.
excerpt: PwC's US CEO says the firm is hiring fewer junior consultants and accountants and more data scientists, as its AI Jobs Barometer shows a 42% pay gap opening up.
content_html:
The Big Four built its fortune on armies of junior consultants and accountants. PwC has started hiring fewer of them. Its US boss says that is the future, and he is comfortable with it.

Paul Griggs, PwC’s US senior partner and chief executive, told Business Insider the firm hired fewer consultants and accountants this year than it did two years ago. He expects that to hold as PwC takes on more data scientists, engineers and machine-learning experts. Last August, an internal deck showed the firm trimming its US campus-hiring targets three years running.

PwC’s own research explains the shift. Its 2026 AI Jobs Barometer, drawn from more than a billion job postings, found professional-services roles among the fastest to change. Jobs that demand more human expertise are growing twice as fast as those where AI lets novices do the work. Pay in the expertise-heavy roles has risen 42% faster since 2021.

The pyramid loses its base

This is a quiet rewiring of how the firm works. Consulting has long run on a pyramid: cheap junior staff at the bottom, expensive partners at the top. Strip out the base and the economics change. Griggs insists the core work in accounting, consulting and finance has not fundamentally changed. What has changed is who gets hired to do it.

The new hire looks different. Griggs says PwC is recruiting more people from nontraditional backgrounds, and expects more liberal-arts graduates, because AI raises the value of broad knowledge. He is a self-described big believer in master’s degrees, and would back his own children through an MBA. The firm still recruits from those programmes, and built an AI-era leadership course with Harvard for 4,000 partners.

The CEO’s own tell

The most revealing detail is personal. Griggs has three children, two still in college. Two of them may go into consulting, and he says he is all for it. The man hiring fewer consultants is pointing his own kids toward the job.

His optimism is not pure spin. Griggs says AI creates value, value drives growth, and growth creates fresh demand for people and tools. He calls PwC’s new-business pipeline the strongest in its history. The moment, he says, is “the biggest opportunity” the firm has ever had.

There is a colder reading. Every consultancy now sells AI transformation, and PwC is remaking itself in the image it markets. Fewer junior desks means fewer people learning the trade from the bottom up. The pipeline may be full today. The harder question is who staffs it in ten years, once the entry rungs are gone.

content_html_zh:
四大公司的财富建立在大批初级顾问和会计师的基础上。 普华永道已开始减少招聘人员。 其美国老板表示，这就是未来，他对此感到满意。

普华永道美国高级合伙人兼首席执行官保罗·格里格斯（Paul Griggs）告诉《商业内幕》，该公司今年雇用的顾问和会计师比两年前要少。 他预计，随着普华永道聘请更多数据科学家、工程师和机器学习专家，这种情况将会持续下去。 去年八月，一份内部报告显示，该公司连续三年削减了美国校园的招聘目标。

普华永道自己的研究解释了这种转变。 其 2026 年人工智能就业晴雨表从超过 10 亿个职位发布中得出，发现专业服务职位是变化最快的职位之一。 需要更多人类专业知识的工作增长速度是人工智能让新手完成工作的工作的两倍。 自 2021 年以来，专业知识密集型职位的薪酬增长了 42%。

金字塔失去了基础

这是对公司运作方式的悄然重新调整。 咨询业长期以来一直在金字塔上运行：廉价的初级员工在底部，昂贵的合作伙伴在顶部。 去掉基础，经济就会发生变化。 格里格斯坚称，会计、咨询和财务方面的核心工作并未发生根本性变化。 改变的是谁被雇用来做这件事。

新员工看起来有所不同。 格里格斯表示，普华永道正在招聘更多非传统背景的人才，并预计会有更多文科毕业生，因为人工智能提高了广泛知识的价值。 他自称是硕士学位的坚定拥护者，并会支持自己的孩子攻读 MBA。 该公司仍在从这些项目中招募人才，并与哈佛大学合作为 4,000 名合作伙伴开设了人工智能时代的领导力课程。

首席执行官自己的说法

最能揭示人性的细节是个人的。 格里格斯有三个孩子，其中两个还在上大学。 其中两人可能会进入咨询行业，他说他完全赞成。 减少聘请顾问的人是在引导自己的孩子接受这份工作。

他的乐观并非纯粹的虚构。 格里格斯表示，人工智能创造价值，价值推动增长，而增长又为人员和工具创造新的需求。 他称普华永道的新业务渠道是其历史上最强大的。 他说，这一刻是该公司曾经拥有的“最大的机会”。

有一种更冷的阅读。 现在每家咨询公司都在推销人工智能转型，而普华永道正在按照其营销的形象重塑自己。 初级办公桌越少，意味着自下而上学习这一行业的人就越少。 今天管道可能已满。 更困难的问题是，一旦入门梯级消失，十年后谁将负责它。
